prerequisites: Ability to grasp complex dependencies and interaction patterns

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have acquired comprehensive knowledge in Boolean algebra, structure and functioning of basic digital circuits, cost optimization of digital function groups, techniques for clock-synchronous data processing, coding and processing of data, structure and functioning of basic functionalities that are central components especially in microprocessor architectures.
Students are able to understand basic circuit concepts of digital logic and function blocks, analyze their interaction, evaluate their functionality, and develop simple blocks themselves.
Evaluation and development of multi-stage combinatorial logic blocks and Finite State Machines (FSMs) will be covered.
Students will learn the hardware description language Verilog, and Verilog examples will be given for each topic of the lecture.
The lecture deals exclusively with (clock-)synchronous circuits.

teaching_methods: Exercises (on computer or with pen and paper)
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the exam. The exam grade contributes 5/150 to the final grade for B.Sc. IT-Security/Information Technology [PO 22].
